current.text: He is projected to start in the backcourt at shooting guard next to Mikel Brown Jr. The Nets do not see him as a full-time point guard, and he will play both on and off the ball.
He will handle the ball less with Julius Randle in Brooklyn, because Randle will handle the ball a lot.
At best he is the third offensive option and competes for touches. Josh expects his usage to rise only a little, from 19.5 to about 20 or 21, with better efficiency.
The Nets see him as a key piece and expect a second-year leap as an on-ball creator and interior scorer. That could open up more pick and roll playmaking.
In summer league he averaged 19 and 5 and hit 76% on six two-pointers a game. He drove more and hit mid-range shots but could not hit threes.
He dealt with a foot issue last season and finished outside the top 200 (230th in categories).
Josh projects him around 120th with a wide range and upside of about 80th, which makes him a round 10 to 11 pick.
Josh calls him his best upside target in all formats for year two. Another expert sees him as a solid late flyer.
Brooklyn does not own its pick, so it has no reason to tank. Second-half minutes are uncertain, and the team could hand more development minutes to young players including Demin.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. With a March 28 end, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3, so 10 games, with one back-to-back in the playoff weeks.

durable.text: As a rookie he was mostly a three-point shooter. He hit 39% on about six threes a game, took only about two twos a game and made 43% of them, rarely got to the line and shot under 40% from the field.
At BYU he was a point guard with big passing numbers who could not shoot.
His defensive stats are poor and he is not a big rebounder.

note: The market has him on the edge of our 144-player pool (Yahoo rank 143 at 0 USD, ESPN rank 107 at 2 USD), while Josh projects him around 120th with upside near 80th. That makes him a cheap 1 to 2 USD end-of-draft flyer for teams that want threes, though his FG% is a real risk. Early on, check whether he starts, whether his summer-league two-point volume holds up and lifts his FG% above last season's 39.9%, and how many assists he gets next to Randle. Keep in mind the weak 3-4-3 playoff schedule.
